sections.h2: What the Douglas County recording office does
sections.html:
Permanent public documents, mostly real estate records, are recorded, indexed, copied and preserved by the Recording Division. Colorado law puts the deeds and mortgages behind each house sale in the county under that umbrella. The same office also issues marriage and civil union licenses, books first-time passport appointments and posts special district public notices.

When you sell, your closing agent records the deed here. That recorded document joins the public chain of title that the next owner and lender will rely on.

A free fraud detection service from the division sends you an alert any time a document is recorded under your name or on your property. It is aimed at title theft, where someone records a false deed. Sign up if you own a vacant house, a rental or an inherited property that nobody visits often, because a bad filing on an empty house can sit unnoticed for months.

Register before you list and leave the alert on while a sale is pending, so you can watch your own deed hit the record. If an alert shows a filing you don't recognize, phone the Clerk and Recorder and your title company right away. A quick call costs far less than untangling a bad deed after a sale falls through.

The county offices are on Wilcox Street in Castle Rock. For hand delivery and the other basics:

  • Street address: 301 Wilcox Street, Castle Rock, CO 80104.
  • Mailing address: P.O. Box 1360, Castle Rock, CO 80104.
  • Land records hours: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Checks are payable to Douglas County Clerk & Recorder.

Electronic recording goes through a county-approved vendor and is offered to high-volume businesses, so individuals file on paper. At most closings the title or escrow company sends the deed, which means a seller rarely carries a document to the counter.

Recording a standard document costs $43 per document, and the state documentary fee is added based on the sale price.

Document typeFee
Standard document (8.5 x 14 to 24 x 36)$43 per document
Land survey plat$50
UCC filing, 1 to 2 pages$13
UCC filing, 3 or more pages$18
Death certificates and DD-214Free
State documentary fee$0.01 per $100 if consideration is over $500

Technology surcharges are already built into the county's fees, and the documentary fee is the only charge that tracks the sale price. Amounts can change, so confirm with the office before you send payment.

sections.h2: Getting a deed ready to record
sections.html:
Before anything goes in the mail, read the county's published checklist of recording requirements. In practice, a seller can:

  • Let the closing or title company prepare and submit the deed.
  • Check that the legal description matches your prior deed.
  • Keep the recorded copy and its reception number for your files.
  • Ask the office for a copy if none arrives.

A rejected document can push back a closing date. That is one reason an experienced title company makes a straightforward cash sale move faster.

A change of ownership is one trigger for a Notice of Value, so a recorded sale can lead the Assessor to send the new owner a notice. Douglas County sends notices only where value, use or ownership changed, which is fewer than 10% of owners. Notices go out May 1 and written objections are due June 8. Business personal property appeals run June 15 through June 30.

  • Assessor's Office: 301 Wilcox Street, Castle Rock, 303-660-7450.
  • County general information: 303-660-7400.

If you sell during appeal season, tell the buyer which valuation notices you received so they know what is pending.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the recorded deed
sections.html:
A lien from unpaid tax doesn't disappear because the deed changes hands. Unpaid taxes can reach the November tax lien sale held by the Treasurer, where the buyer receives a lien, not the property. The interest rate is nine points above the federal discount rate as of September 1, and the current rate is 13%. A deed actually transfers in less than 1 percent of purchases.

Ask your title company to run a tax check before the deed is signed. Any balance gets paid from proceeds, and the recorded deed goes in clean. Property tax is separate from recording, but a sale usually settles both at the same closing.

Here is what usually happens once you sign.

  1. The title or escrow company sends the deed to the Recording Division with the $43 fee and the documentary fee.
  2. The office indexes the document, and it becomes part of the public chain of title.
  3. The Assessor may mail the new owner a Notice of Value because ownership changed.
  4. You keep the recorded copy and its reception number with your closing papers.

If the recorded deed doesn't turn up when you expect it, call the Clerk and Recorder's office and ask for the reception number, then check with your title company. Nothing needs to be re-signed in most cases, since the company holds the original paperwork. Compare the legal description on the new deed with your prior deed before closing day, and ask the title officer to walk you through the other items in the county's checklist so a rejected filing does not delay the sale. Keep copies of everything you sign.

Recording covers the deeds and mortgages for real estate in the county, whatever the type of sale, and an inherited house is no exception. A title company usually prepares and submits the paperwork for you. Heirs should expect the title search to look at every recorded document on the property, so gather any older deeds, loan papers and tax statements you can find before you list.

Vacant inherited houses are the ones the fraud alert helps most. Sign up as soon as you take over, even if you plan to sell in a few weeks.

sections.h2: State programs that affect a seller's taxes
sections.html: Colorado lists a property tax rebate, deferral, work-off program, senior exemption and a veteran with a disability exemption. Residential property is taxed at two state-set rates for 2026: 6.8% for local governments and 7.05% for schools. The revenue stays in the county and supports schools, counties, special districts, municipalities and junior colleges. Questions go to the state Division of Property Taxation at (303) 864-7777.

sections.h2: Why recorded records matter near creeks and open space
sections.html: Highlands Ranch is the largest community in the county, and Castle Rock, Parker, Lone Tree and Castle Pines also generate many recordings. Land near creeks and open space is often described in recorded easements, which is another reason the recorded record matters when you sell. Ask the title company to include any easements in the package you hand the buyer.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in Douglas County, Colorado?
faqs.a: The Douglas County Clerk and Recorder's Recording Division, in Castle Rock.

faqs.q: Is there free fraud protection for Douglas County property?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recording Division offers a free alert service that tells you when a document is recorded in your name or on your property.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee in Douglas County?
faqs.a: $43 per standard document, plus the state documentary fee of $0.01 per $100 of consideration over $500.

faqs.q: Can individuals e-record in Douglas County?
faqs.a: No. Electronic recording is for high-volume businesses through an approved vendor, so individuals use paper or a title company.

faqs.q: What are the land records hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., at 301 Wilcox Street, Castle Rock. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1360, Castle Rock, CO 80104, with checks payable to Douglas County Clerk & Recorder.
